changes: Added a hard rule at the top of `/agent/solver.md` forbidding `submit` until the solver has run the public examples, compared its fast solution against a brute force on random small inputs, and timed it at a large size. Most dev failures were submitted after 2–3 model calls with zero or one test run, so the existing verification steps were being skipped. I also added a short list of common mistakes to check (off-by-one, counting start states, constraints on intermediate states, double counting in cycles or components). One trial on lcb-3655 still failed: the solver ran the examples and timing but skipped the brute-force comparison, which is the check that would likely have caught the wrong answer. I did not add a skill or sub-agent and did not run further trials.
final:
The change is in place and validates, but the one trial I ran still failed, so I'm predicting a small gain rather than a large one.
